children: InnovAge Holding Corp. reported full-year 2026 revenue of $989.71M, up 15.9% from $853.7M a year earlier, and a net loss narrowing to ($2.54M) from ($30.31M) in 2025; diluted loss per share improved to ($0.02) from ($0.22). The results reflect membership growth, higher capitation rates and expense actions taken during the year.
¹ Reported as “Total revenues”. ² Reported as “Net Loss Attributable to InnovAge Holding Corp.”. ³ Reported as “loss per share - diluted”.
Revenue growth was driven by capitation: capitation revenue increased 16% year‑over‑year due to 7.8% member‑month growth and 7.6% higher rates.
The company transitioned pharmacy services in‑house, lowering external pharmacy costs and improving per‑participant expense.
InnovAge remains the largest U.S. PACE provider with about 8,230 participants across 20 centers and continues expansion in California, Colorado, Florida, New Mexico, Pennsylvania and Virginia.
Operational efficiency initiatives and investments in clinical and operational value programs increased center-level leverage, lifting contribution margin to roughly 23% of revenue.

Management noted regulatory and operational milestones including converting two Pennsylvania centers to alternate care settings, remediating California audit findings and pursuing a Bakersfield de novo center.
